acceptance.criterion: The Root is a native Prefect Flow Run and completes a two-Stage invocation.
acceptance.evidence: Five of five Root Flow Runs completed.

acceptance.criterion: Two independently registered Stage Deployments are invoked from each Root invocation.
acceptance.evidence: Ten Stage Deployment Flow Runs across five Root invocations; both deployment names are recorded in each Root result.

acceptance.criterion: The qualified work pool contains exactly the two expected ONLINE Process Workers before execution.
acceptance.evidence: The qualification script checked the exact ONLINE worker set before the batch: gpwcf-stage-worker-01 and gpwcf-stage-worker-02.

acceptance.criterion: Sibling Stage Deployments execute on distinct Process Worker instances.
acceptance.evidence: Distinct worker labels were recorded and validated for both Stages in all five Root invocations.

acceptance.criterion: Sibling Stage Flow Run execution intervals overlap in repeated runs.
acceptance.evidence: Positive overlap in five of five runs; see PHASE-02_Repeatability_Evidence.json.

acceptance.criterion: The Stage Flow Run identity matches the Deployment Flow Run identity.
acceptance.evidence: Validated for all ten Stage Flow Runs.

acceptance.criterion: Stage Flow Run native parent_task_run_id matches the Prefect-generated deployment invocation Task Run.
acceptance.evidence: Validated for all ten Stage Flow Runs.

acceptance.criterion: The synthetic deployment invocation Task Run links back to the correct Root dispatch Task Run.
acceptance.evidence: task_inputs.__parents__ links verified for all ten Stage invocations.

acceptance.criterion: Stage identity, Stage invocation identity and Pipeline invocation identity remain separate from Prefect operational IDs.
acceptance.evidence: Domain correlation fields and Prefect Flow/Task Run IDs are independently recorded and compared in all runs.

acceptance.criterion: The Stage Deployment returns a persisted domain result that the Root can retrieve.
acceptance.evidence: persist_result=True; both Stage results were loaded by the Root in all five invocations (ten Stage results).

acceptance.criterion: Stage-to-Step native Subflow boundaries and parent correlations remain intact.
acceptance.evidence: Twenty Step Subflow invocations; each synthetic child-subflow Task links to its Stage-owned Step dispatch Task.

acceptance.criterion: SPU Tasks execute within their owning Step Flow Run and the Stage does not bypass the Step boundary.
acceptance.evidence: Forty SPU Task Runs across the five Root invocations; SPU flow_run_id matches the owning Step Flow Run.

acceptance.criterion: SPUExecutionResult and StepExecutionResult remain distinct from Prefect State.
acceptance.evidence: Typed fixture results are returned in the Stage domain result; Prefect State is recorded separately.

acceptance.criterion: The deployment code source and result storage are accessible to workers on a different host.
acceptance.evidence: This qualification uses same-host LocalStorage and local result storage under PREFECT_HOME.

acceptance.criterion: Production GPWCF Stage/Step/SPU classes are bound to Prefect Deployments.
acceptance.evidence: Contract-shaped fixtures only; no production GPWCF classes were modified or bound.

acceptance.criterion: Deployment failure, cancellation, timeout, retry and worker restart semantics are qualified.
acceptance.evidence: Success-path deployment invocation only; failure and lifecycle settlement remain follow-up work.

phaseDisposition: The same-host two-Process-Worker deployment profile qualifies concurrent sibling Stage Flow execution, native identity correlation, indirect parent linkage, Stage result retrieval and preservation of the existing Step/SPU hierarchy. It does not qualify multi-host storage, production GPWCF binding, failure/cancellation/recovery semantics or capacity beyond two concurrent Stages.
